Usage: drive park <view> <reason> ... [flags]

Stop a session's wakes until a step is sent to it, keeping why.

A parked session sends no wakes until a step is sent to it, so a session
waiting on the owner, on another session's hold, or for a date stops waking
the driver. Something on record has to end the park, or it is refused: an
open ask about the session (drive record ask), a hold it was refused a step
for, or --until. An ask answered with no step leaves the park with nothing
to end it, and a time past its --until comes due: status lists either under
the table, and the watchdog wakes the driver about it once.

Arguments:
  <view>               The view the park was decided on.
  <reason> ...         Why it waits, in the owner's terms; the record keeps it and the owner's page
                       shows it.

Flags:
      --until=WHEN     When to look at it again: a date or a date and time in the batch's zone, such
                       as 2026-11-06 or "2026-11-06 09:00", or a duration such as 4h. The watchdog
                       wakes you about it then.

Inherited flags:
  -h, --help           Show context-sensitive help.
      --batch=NAME     Act in this batch, as drive prints its name, instead of the driver's current
                       one. It may stand anywhere on the line.
      --driver=NAME    Act in the batch this driver drives now; a chat driver's name is its
                       webhook's. It may stand anywhere on the line.

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    refused: nothing was done; next: says what to run instead
  2    invalid arguments; nothing was run
  3    tried and did not end as asked; the message says what did happen
  4    the session's login was rejected; next: relaunches it on another account, or says to tell the
       owner
